info.title: plumbline API
info.summary: Scan websites in the browser, and keep domains, their checks and their reports.
info.description:
The REST contract under `/api` follows the [Zalando RESTful API Guidelines](https://opensource.zalando.com/restful-api-guidelines/) with the deviations in the `api-design` skill: JSON properties are snake_case, timestamps are RFC 3339, and every error is `application/problem+json`.

The checks run on the server, in a scanner container. The page starts a scan here, which checks the address and signs a scan id, and then asks for the run, which streams each check as it finishes. Nothing is stored: the id carries the address and when the scan ends, signed so it cannot be made up.

Scanning and the list of checks are public. Keeping domains, choosing their checks, saving reports and the account need a sign-in with Google (`/auth/login`), which sets the `plumbline_session` cookie; those routes declare `session` security, answer `401` without a live session, and `403` for a request that changes something from another site. Every query is scoped to the signed-in person, so another person's domain is `404`.

Requests are rate limited by the platform (`RL_SCAN` for starting scans and running them, per address; `RL_API` for the rest of `/api`), and a blocked request is answered with `429` and `Retry-After`. On top of that one page (its canonical URL) can be scanned once every five minutes, by anyone; a second scan within that time is `429` with `Retry-After` set to the seconds left.

Only the REST contract under `/api` is described here. What is not REST sits outside it and is not part of the contract: the browser sign-in and link flows (`/auth/*`), the OAuth server (`/oauth/*`, `/.well-known/*`), the MCP endpoint (`/mcp`), the live stream (`/events`), the GitHub webhook (`/webhooks/github`), the badge image (`/badge/*`), the report pages (`/r/{id}`), `/csp/reports` and `/health`.

Testing the whole contract as an ordinary person: every operation here can be called by one signed-in account, with its session cookie. There is no administrator role and no operation that needs one, so a test account sees nothing it could not see in the app.

tags.name: previews
tags.description: What the checks on pull requests found.

post.summary: Start a scan of a website.
post.description: Checks the address, puts it in its canonical form (lowercase host without a trailing dot, no default port, fragment or repeated slashes, no `utm_*` or click-id parameters, the rest of the query sorted by name) and signs a scan id for it, good for ten minutes. A page can be scanned once every five minutes; a second scan within that time is refused with `429`. Nothing else is stored and there is nothing to read back; the id is for the scan's run.

post.summary: Run the checks of a scan on the server.
post.description: Has the scanner container run every check on the scan's address and streams the result as newline-delimited JSON: a `ready` line with the final address, its status and the list of checks, a `done` line with the outcome of each check as it finishes, then `end`. When the page does not answer the stream is a single `unreachable` line with a `detail`, then `end`. A scan's id runs the checks once.

200.description: The checks, one line of JSON each, as they finish.

404.description: No such scan, or it has ended.

get.summary: What a check on a pull request found.
get.description: Public, so a tool that finds a failed check can read it without signing in; the random id in the address, which the check links to, is the only key. It is made once for a commit and never changes, so it is kept by its id, never by age.

post.summary: Read the person's GitHub installations again.
post.description: Reads the installations of the app the person connected, so repositories added since, and changes to where they are deployed, show up.

502.description: GitHub could not be read for any installation; the detail says why.

delete.description: Forgets the account, its installations and the repositories found. Domains already added stay, and the app stays installed on GitHub until it is uninstalled there.

get.summary: The key a browser subscribes to Web Push with.

post.summary: Turn notifications on for a browser.
post.description: Registers the browser's Web Push subscription for the person. Registering the same endpoint again replaces its keys (browsers rotate them) and its owner (a device can change hands).

delete.summary: Turn notifications off for a browser.

post.summary: Send a test notification to a browser.

502.description: The push service refused the notification.

get.summary: List every check plumbline can run.

parameters.name: group
parameters.description: Only the checks in this group (a source such as `owasp`, or a topic such as `tls`).

200.description: A page of checks, sorted by id.

get.summary: List the signed-in person's domains, oldest first.

post.summary: Add a domain, with every check on.

200.description: The person already has this domain; it is returned unchanged, with its `Location`.

409.description: The person already keeps the most domains allowed (50).

get.summary: Read one domain and the checks that run for it.

patch.summary: Choose which checks run for a domain.

parameters.name: If-Match
parameters.description: The domain's `ETag`; the change is refused with `412` when the domain changed since.

200.description: The domain as it now is.

412.description: The domain changed since the `ETag` in `If-Match`.

delete.summary: Remove a domain and its saved reports.

get.summary: List a domain's saved reports, newest first, without their outcomes.

post.summary: Save the outcome of a scan that has just run in the browser.
post.description: Only the newest 20 reports of a domain are kept. The counts are worked out from the outcomes.

get.summary: Read one saved report with every check's outcome.

delete.summary: Delete the account with its domains, reports and connected apps, and sign out.

get.summary: List the assistants the person has connected over MCP.

200.description: A page of connected apps, newest first.

delete.summary: Disconnect an assistant, revoking its tokens at once.
Sign out everywhere, on every device.

204.description: Signed out (also when nobody was signed in).

url.description: A domain (`example.com`) or an absolute http(s) URL. A missing scheme means `https`. IP addresses, `localhost` and private names are refused.

id.description: The scan's id, for its run.

expires_at.description: When the scan's run stops being accepted.

fixer.description: Who usually makes the fix, such as the web server's configuration or the DNS zone.

origins.description: The upstream checks this one was taken from; empty for a check written for plumbline.

next.description: The next page; absent on the last one.

host.description: A public domain, or any http(s) URL on it.

checks.description: The checks to run, as check ids and group names, or `null` for every check (including ones added later).

all_checks.description: Whether every check runs, including ones added later.

checks.description: The ids of the checks that run.

links.description: Further reading for this finding, besides the check's own reference.

reason.description: Why a skipped check did not run.

url.description: The address that was scanned, on the domain's host.

Connection.description: An assistant the person approved over MCP.

id.description: The lower-case hex SHA-256 of the endpoint.

Unauthorized.description: Nobody is signed in, or the session has ended.

Forbidden.description: A request that changes something came from another site.

NotFound.description: The signed-in person has no such resource.

BadRequest.description: The body is not a JSON object, or a field is missing or not valid; `errors` names each.

TooManyRequests.description: Too many requests from this address; wait for `Retry-After` seconds.

NotConfigured.description: The server has no secret to sign scans with.

Limit.name: limit
Limit.description: The most items on a page (1 to 100, default 20).

Cursor.name: cursor
Cursor.description: Where the page starts, from the previous page's `next` link.

Location.description: The absolute address of the resource.

session.name: plumbline_session
session.description: The signed session cookie set by signing in with Google at `/auth/login`.
